chapters.title: Chapter 1: What TDS Is and How It Works

lessons.title: TDS Under the Income-tax Act, 2025: The Tax Year and What Changed

body.text: On 1 April 2026, the rules of TDS barely moved. The addresses did. Rates, thresholds and deadlines largely carried over, but the section numbers, form numbers, payment codes and even the name of the year you are taxed for all changed.

children.text: Sanjay, a marketing manager in Ahmedabad, opened a TDS certificate from his bank in July 2026 and stopped. Where he expected "Section 194A", it said "Section 393". His payroll portal talked about "tax year 2026-27" instead of "assessment year". His colleague's Form 15H had apparently become something called Form 121. Nothing about his salary or his fixed deposit had changed, yet every label had.

This lesson is your translation guide. It covers why India replaced its income tax law, what "tax year" means, where every TDS rule you have learnt so far now lives, and how to tell which law applies to a payment made around the changeover.
A New Law After 64 Years

The Income-tax Act, 1961 had been amended so many times that it had grown to more than 800 sections, many with lettered sub-sections like 194-IA and 194BA that existed only because new rules had been squeezed in between old ones. The Income-tax Act, 2025 rewrites the same law in plainer language, groups related provisions together and replaces long paragraphs with tables and formulas. Its stated aim is simplification, not a change in the tax burden.

body.title: Old law vs new law: how much shorter the rulebook got

events.title: First Bill introduced
events.description: The Income-tax Bill, 2025 was introduced in the Lok Sabha and sent to a Select Committee for review.

events.title: Revised Bill passed by Lok Sabha
events.description: After incorporating the committee's suggestions, the government withdrew the first Bill and introduced the Income-tax (No. 2) Bill, 2025, which the Lok Sabha passed the same day.

events.title: Presidential assent
events.description: The Bill became the Income-tax Act, 2025.

events.title: New Rules and forms
events.description: The Income-tax Rules, 2026 were notified with renumbered forms for TDS certificates, statements and declarations.

events.title: New Act takes effect
events.description: The Income-tax Act, 1961 is repealed. Income earned up to 31 March 2026 is still assessed under the old Act through savings and transition provisions, and tax year 2026-27 is the first under the new one.

children.text: The Tax Year: One Term Instead of Two

markDefs.definition: The 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March in which income is earned and for which it is taxed. For a business or source of income that starts mid-year, the first tax year runs from the start date to the following 31 March.

children.text: Under the old law, income earned in a "previous year" was taxed in the following "assessment year". Salary earned from April 2025 to March 2026 belonged to previous year 2025-26 and assessment year 2026-27. Generations of taxpayers found this confusing. The new Act replaces both with a single
tax year
: the year you earn the income is the year you name.

columns.label: Income-tax Act, 1961
points: Income earned: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026
Called previous year (or financial year) 2025-26
Taxed in assessment year 2026-27
Return filed in 2026 under the 1961 Act

columns.label: Income-tax Act, 2025
points: Income earned: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027
Called tax year 2026-27
No separate assessment year
Return filed in 2027 under the 2025 Act

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Name the Year
body.textWithBlank: Interest your bank credits to your FD in December 2026 is part of your income for tax year ___.
body.explanation: December 2026 falls between 1 April 2026 and 31 March 2027, so it belongs to tax year 2026-27. Under the old vocabulary, that would have been previous year 2026-27 and assessment year 2027-28.

body.text: Both vocabularies will be around for a while. The return you filed in 2026 for income earned in 2025-26 was still under the 1961 Act, so it used assessment year 2026-27. Returns, notices and refunds for earlier years keep the old terms. Check which Act a document refers to before comparing years.

children.text: Where TDS Lives Now

The old Act spread TDS across dozens of separate sections from 192 to 196D, each with its own rate, threshold and exceptions. The new Act collects them into a small cluster of sections. The two you will see most are Section 392 for salary and Section 393 for everything else.

Certificates for lower or nil deduction

children.text: Tables instead of lettered sections

Inside Section 393, each type of payment is a numbered row in a table that lists who pays, the rate and the threshold. So a citation that used to be a single section number now has three parts: the sub-section, the table and the serial number.

body.title: Quick Check: Find the New Home
body.question: A listed company deducts TDS on the dividend it pays you in September 2026. Which provision of the Income-tax Act, 2025 governs that deduction?
body.explanation: Dividends are a non-salary payment, so they fall under the tables in Section 393, replacing old Section 194. Section 392 is salary, Section 394 is TCS, and Section 397(2) only matters if you did not furnish a valid PAN.

body.title: Why challans now use payment codes instead of section numbers

children.text: Under the old Act, a deductor paying TDS on professional fees would pick "194J" on the challan and in the quarterly statement. Since the new Act has no Section 194J, TDS challans and statements for payments from 1 April 2026 use four-digit nature of payment codes instead, one for each row of the new tables. A few old sections are split into several codes, for example separate codes for bank interest paid to senior citizens and to others.

For you as a deductee, the practical point is this: if a deductor picks the wrong code, your credit can land under the wrong type of income in AIS, or the statement can be flagged as defective. When an entry in your AIS looks mislabelled, the code is one of the first things to query with the deductor.
The Forms You Know, Renumbered
The Income-tax Rules, 2026 gave the TDS forms new numbers. Many people will keep using the old names in conversation for years, so learn both.

cards.definition: Now Form 130. Annual TDS certificate for salary, issued by the employer.
Now Form 131. Quarterly TDS certificate for non-salary payments.
Now Form 138. Employer's quarterly TDS statement for salary.
Now Form 140. Quarterly TDS statement for non-salary payments to residents.
Now Form 144. Quarterly TDS statement for payments to non-residents.
Now a single Form 141. PAN-based challan-cum-statement for property, rent, large contractor payments and crypto.
Now Form 168. Annual tax credit statement against your PAN.
Now a single Form 121. Self-declaration for no TDS when your tax liability is nil, for any eligible age.

body.text: The Form 16 you received in June 2026 was for salary earned in 2025-26 under the old Act, so it kept its old name. The first Form 130 arrives by 15 June 2027, for salary paid in tax year 2026-27.

children.text: What Changed and What Did Not

columns.label: Changed
points: Section numbers: 392 for salary, 393 for other payments
Form numbers for certificates, statements and declarations
Nature of payment codes on challans and statements
"Tax year" replaces previous year and assessment year
Forms 15G and 15H merged into Form 121

columns.label: Largely unchanged
points: Deposit by the 7th of the next month, 30 April for March
Quarterly statement due dates: 31 July, 31 October, 31 January, 31 May
Rates and thresholds, such as 10% on FD interest above ₹50,000 (₹1,00,000 for seniors)
Higher TDS of generally 20% without a valid PAN
Interest of 1% and 1.5% a month on TDS defaults

body.title: Try It: Same Rule, New Section
body.prompt: Deepak, 67, a retired railway officer in Lucknow, earns ₹1,40,000 of FD interest from Bank of Baroda in tax year 2026-27 and has not submitted Form 121. How much TDS does the bank deduct?
body.explanation: The senior citizen threshold of ₹1,00,000 and the 10% rate carried over into Section 393. His interest crosses the threshold, so TDS applies to the whole ₹1,40,000: 10% is ₹14,000. Only the section on his certificate changed, from 194A to 393.

children.text: Around the Changeover: Which Law Applies?

For non-salary payments, the test is the same one you met in Lesson 1: look at whichever came first, the credit in the payer's books or the actual payment. If that earlier event was on or before 31 March 2026, the 1961 Act governs the deduction. If it was on or after 1 April 2026, the 2025 Act governs it. For salary, TDS is tied to the date of payment.

cells: Form 24Q or 26Q for January to March 2026
Form 138 or 140 from April to June 2026 onwards

body.title: Scenario: Three Payments Around 1 April
body.scenario: A Kochi-based design studio (a private limited company) deals with three payments. First, it receives a consultant's invoice for ₹1,20,000, books it as payable on 25 March 2026 and pays it on 10 April 2026. Second, it books and pays a ₹90,000 fee to a freelance illustrator on 15 April 2026. Third, it pays April salaries on 30 April 2026.
body.prompt: For each payment, which Act governs TDS, and which statement form will it appear in?
body.modelAnswer: Payment 1: the credit on 25 March 2026 came before the payment, so the 1961 Act applies. TDS falls under old Section 194J, must be deposited by 30 April 2026 (the March deadline), and is reported in Form 26Q for January to March 2026, with Form 16A as the certificate. Payment 2: both credit and payment fall after 1 April 2026, so Section 393 of the 2025 Act applies. It is reported in Form 140 for April to June 2026, with Form 131 as the certificate. Payment 3: salary paid on 30 April 2026 falls under Section 392 of the 2025 Act and is reported in Form 138 for April to June 2026. The employees will receive Form 130 for tax year 2026-27 by 15 June 2027.

children.text: Update Your Own Toolkit

body.title: Switch to the New Vocabulary
steps: Write "tax year 2026-27" on any tax folder, spreadsheet or tracker for income from April 2026 onwards
Keep a copy of the old-to-new form list from this lesson where you store your tax documents
If you are eligible for nil TDS on interest or dividends, submit Form 121 to each bank or company at the start of tax year 2027-28
When your bank or broker issues a TDS certificate for 2026-27, confirm it cites Section 393, not an old section number
Expect Form 130, not Form 16, from your employer by 15 June 2027

cards.definition: The 1 April to 31 March period in which income is earned and taxed. Replaces previous year and assessment year.
TDS on salary and accumulated PF withdrawals. Formerly Sections 192 and 192A.
TDS on all other payments, organised in tables. Formerly Sections 193 to 196D.
Tax collected at source. Formerly Section 206C.
Lower or nil deduction certificates. Formerly Section 197.
TAN, higher TDS without PAN and TDS statements. Formerly Sections 203A, 206AA and 200.
Consequences of TDS defaults, including interest. Formerly Section 201.
A deductee cannot be asked to pay tax already deducted from them. Formerly Section 205.

points: The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026, cutting the law from 819 sections to 536 and the Rules from 511 to 333
A single "tax year" replaces previous year and assessment year. Income from April 2026 to March 2027 is tax year 2026-27
TDS on salary is now Section 392, TDS on other payments is Section 393 (organised as tables) and TCS is Section 394
Key forms were renumbered: Form 16 is Form 130, Form 16A is Form 131, Form 26AS is Form 168 and Forms 15G and 15H became Form 121
Rates, thresholds and deposit and statement deadlines largely carried over unchanged
For non-salary payments, the earlier of credit or payment decides which Act applies. Anything on or before 31 March 2026 stays under the 1961 Act
